list: The official 55 trophies, 1 platinum, 2 gold, 6 silver, 46 bronze, as listed before this guide was written.

sources.exophase: Official trophy list as published on Exophase — the source for every trophy's name, description and grade in this file.
sources.psnprofiles: PSNProfiles trophy list — the source for PSN's progress counts (such as 42 Shooting Range challenges) wherever a count is given.
sources.own: Own advice built from the official description alone. The game launched on 2026-11-19, so a step that goes beyond the description is labelled as not yet checked in the game — no location or trick is claimed as verified where the description does not say it.

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: The platinum is the reward for everything else: it pops the moment the other 54 trophies are earned, with no extra task of its own. Treat it as a progress bar, not a job — work the roadmap stages in order and it arrives on its own. The last trophy you earn will almost certainly be A Long Road (100% completion) or one of the big grinds, so plan your cleanup around those, not around this one.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: Finish the opening mission, Gone Fishing — the first mission of the game, so this is the first trophy most players earn. Nothing to prepare and nothing to miss: play the story from the start and it pops when the mission ends. If you are replaying missions, the opening mission is the one to pick.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: Play through Chapter 1 to its end; the trophy pops when the chapter closes. Chapters in this game are story blocks, so there is no side content required — just keep following the story missions in order. Unmissable as long as you finish the chapter, and it is the first of four chapter trophies that pace the whole playthrough.

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: Play through Chapter 2 to its end; the trophy pops when the chapter closes. Like the other chapter trophies it only asks that you finish the story block, so keep working the story missions in order and do not worry about side content here. This is the second of the four chapter trophies.

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: Play through Chapter 3 to its end; the trophy pops when the chapter closes. By this point the map and the side activities are wide open, but the chapter trophy itself still only needs the story missions done in order. A good moment to start the long grinds (stunts, vehicles, races) between story missions, since the rest of the game keeps them available.

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: Play through Chapter 4 to its end; the trophy pops when the chapter closes, leaving only the finale. Before you push into the final mission, sweep up anything that needs a story character beside you — partner trophies such as Hot Together and Retail Therapy are easier while the story still pairs you up. Chapter 4 is the last of the four chapter trophies.

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide: Finish the final story mission to earn the game's only story gold. The description names no mission, so this guide does not guess one — it is simply the last mission of the story, and it pops on completion. Before starting it, do a final pass over the partner and choice trophies (Hot Together, Retail Therapy, Actions Speak Louder), because a finale can close off story pairings. Then play the finale and collect the gold.

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Breakfast Run. Named-mission trophies like this one pop on mission completion, whatever your rating or approach, so play it however you like — stealth, speed and style do not matter for the trophy. If a mission can be replayed, a missed trophy can be recovered that way, but the description gives no reason to expect a miss here: finish the mission and it is yours.

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission The Cartel Heist. This is one of the named-mission trophies: finish the mission and it pops, with no extra objective named in the official description. Heists in this series usually offer preparation and approach choices — none of that is required for the trophy, so take the approach you enjoy and let the completion do the work.

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Child's Play. Another named-mission trophy: the official description asks only for completion, so no medal, no time and no optional objective is needed. Play the mission through to its end and the trophy follows.

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Headliners. The trophy pops on mission completion; the official description names nothing else, so there is no hidden objective to hunt for. If you like, use the mission as a chance to practise Combat Focus — you will need it for Gunslinger later — but the mission itself only needs finishing.

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission VCIA Takedown, set at the Vice City airport. The trophy is for finishing the mission, nothing more, and the description does not tie it to a vehicle, a route or a time. Keep it in mind later for Catch Me If You Can — an unscheduled departure at the same airport — since the airport is clearly a place the game wants you to know well.

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Operation Savage Glory. The last of the named-mission trophies: finish the mission and it pops. The name suggests a large set-piece, so go in stocked and expect a fight, but the trophy itself asks only for completion — no medal or optional objective is named in the official description.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: Reach 100% completion — the game's own checklist of story, missions, activities and collectibles — to earn the second gold. This is the real final boss of the platinum: it is only reachable once the story is done and the big counts are finished. Work it last, in Stage 5 of the roadmap, and use the in-game completion screen as your authority on what is still missing; this guide's counts (250 stunts, 100 vehicles, 52 areas) are the pieces the official descriptions name, and they are the pieces that feed this total.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Pull off 250 stunts — jumps, airtime, near misses and the like, as the game counts them. This is a pure grind with no missable moment: every stunt you land anywhere in Leonida counts, so start early and let the number grow while you do everything else. Ramps, jumps and fast driving between missions are the steady way in; check the in-game stunt counter regularly so you know how far along you are, and leave a dedicated stunt session for the final stretch.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try every type of activity once — PSN tracks 9 types. This is the sampler trophy: play one round of each activity the game offers (races, fishing, shooting range, drone races, arcade games, bowling, meditation and the rest) and it pops. Do it early in Stage 2, because each first try also opens up the deeper trophies behind that activity — the Shooting Range feeds The Shootist, the drone races feed Top Fun, and so on.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Earn a gold medal in all 42 Shooting Range challenges — the count is PSN's, and it is the hardest skill trophy on the list. This is the silver that most players will leave until late: learn each challenge's weapon and target pattern, retry freely (challenges can be repeated), and gold them one at a time rather than in one sitting. Accuracy beats speed in most range challenges, so slow down, aim, and treat each gold as its own small win.

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at all 14 locations — the count is PSN's. Each location is its own race, so work through them one by one and tick them off; a win at a location you have already won does not help the next one. Drone racing rewards learning the course, so fly a practice lap first, then race to win. This also feeds Earn Cash, Not Kudos if drone races count among the game's races — check the race counter as you go.

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Win 20 different races — different events, not the same race 20 times. Spread across the race types the game offers (street races, drone races and whatever else the activity list holds) and keep a mental note of which events you have already won. If a race is hard, switch to another event rather than grinding one: breadth is what the trophy counts, and there are more than 20 races to choose from.

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge. Cal is a named rival, so this is a set encounter rather than a grind — take the challenge whenever it is offered and do not put it off, because a rival challenge may not wait around. Fishing challenges are usually about the catch, not the fight, so learn the fishing controls in a free session first, then challenge Cal when you are confident. Flagged missable because the description names a single person and a single challenge, not a repeatable activity.

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: Complete one arcade game — any arcade cabinet, any game, just finish it. The easiest trophy in the activity set: walk up to a cabinet, play to the end of a game and it pops. Pick the shortest or simplest game on offer if you only want the trophy, or play your favourite and enjoy it. This also counts as one of the activity types for Master of None.

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Complete Andy's final mission. Andy is one of the game's side characters with a mission strand of their own: follow their missions to the last one and the trophy pops on completion. Side strands like this are the backbone of Strangers & Freaks, so finishing Andy also moves that silver forward. Do the strand when it appears rather than leaving every side mission for the end.

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Complete Kenton's final mission. Kenton is another side character with a mission strand: work through their missions to the last one and the trophy pops. The name hints at a boat — expect water in this strand — but the trophy asks only for the final mission's completion, so no special approach is required. Finishing Kenton also counts toward the 8 stranger strands of Strangers & Freaks.

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Complete Billy's final mission. Billy's strand is another of the side-character mission lines: follow it to its last mission and the trophy pops on completion. The name suggests riding alone — a bike or a solo run may feature — but the official description asks only that you finish the mission. Like the other character finales, it also advances Strangers & Freaks.

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across Leonida — the side-character lines such as Andy's, Kenton's, Billy's, Randy's and Tyrone's. Each finished strand counts once, so you need eight different strangers, not eight missions for one person. Explore the map, answer the stranger prompts as they appear, and finish each strand when it opens; the counter is per strand, so a half-finished strand earns nothing yet. This is the silver that rewards playing the whole map, not just the story.

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Complete Randy's final mission. Randy is another side character with a mission strand: follow it to its last mission and the trophy pops. The name suggests supply runs, so expect driving and delivery work in this strand, but the trophy only needs the final mission finished. It also counts as one of the 8 stranger strands for Strangers & Freaks.

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Complete Tyrone's final mission. Tyrone is the last of the named side characters with a finale trophy: finish their strand's final mission and it pops. Five character finales (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone) plus the stranger strands make up the side-mission backbone of the game — clear them as they appear and Strangers & Freaks will take care of itself.

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at all 18 spots across Leonida — the count is PSN's. Meditation spots are quiet places scattered over the map, so this is a travelling trophy: visit each spot and meditate there, ticking them off as you go. Pair it with The Goodtime State (explore all of Leonida) and Whip It Good (discover 100 vehicles), since all three reward covering the map, and use the in-game counter to find which spots are still missing.

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Hunt a unique animal for Bret. A unique animal is a one-of-a-kind creature, so this is a single hunt, not a grind — take Bret's job when it appears and do not let the animal get away, because a unique animal may not come back. Go in prepared: track it patiently, take the shot when it is clean, and remember the hunt is the trophy, not the pelt. Flagged missable because the description names one unique animal for one person.

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide: Complete 3 collectible card sets. Cards are hidden around Leonida, and a set is only complete when every card in it is found — so this trophy is really a scavenger hunt with a checklist. Search thoroughly, use the in-game collection screen to see which cards each set is missing, and trade or revisit areas rather than hoping to stumble on the last card. Three full sets is the goal; extra cards beyond that do not add to this trophy.

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide: Use WAiNK It at 100 locations — the game's photo or check-in style collectible, as PSN tracks it. This is the biggest location grind on the list: 100 spots, one action each, spread across the whole map. Fold it into your exploration for The Goodtime State — every new area is a chance to WAiNK It — and keep count in the game so the last few locations are a deliberate sweep, not a blind search.

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide: Complete 50 challenges — the game's own challenge list, which covers feats across combat, driving, activities and exploration. This is a late-game cleanup trophy: by the time the story and the activity trophies are done, the counter will already be well on its way. Check the in-game challenge list, pick off the easy ones first (the ones your normal play has nearly finished), and leave the deliberate ones for a final session.

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: With your partner beside you, build a 4-star wanted level, then lose it and escape. The partner is the catch: this only works while the story has your partner with you, so do it during a story stretch where you fight side by side, before the finale closes those pairings off. Build heat with a crime spree, then break line of sight, hide, and wait for the stars to clear while your partner is still with you. Flagged missable because it needs a partner present at a 4-star moment.

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: With your partner, rob 3 shops in a row without losing your wanted level — the level must stay on through all three robberies. Plan the route first: pick three shops close together, rob each quickly, and keep moving between them so the heat never drops. Like Hot Together it needs your partner beside you, so do it while the story still pairs you up, and do not start the run until the shops and the getaway are picked. Flagged missable for the partner requirement and the unbroken wanted level.

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide: Discover 100 vehicles — drive or ride each one and it counts as discovered. This is a variety trophy, not a mileage one: a new model counts, the same model again does not. Work through traffic, parking lots, garages and the roads between missions, and hop into anything you have not driven yet. Pair it with On the Spot (register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app) and with exploring Leonida for The Goodtime State.

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Take down 5 enemies during one use of Combat Focus — the game's slow-mo aiming mode. Wait for a fight with a crowd of enemies, trigger Combat Focus when several are in view, and chain the takedowns before it ends. Pick a busy mission or a shootout with plenty of cover and plenty of targets, and do not waste the focus on one or two enemies: five in a single use is the whole ask, and the attempt can be retried.

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA, the Vice City airport — leave by a way the airport did not schedule. In plain terms: get a plane (or another aircraft) and take off without following the airport's rules, most likely by stealing one from the tarmac or runway. Expect heavy police attention the moment you do it, so go in fast, pick the first flyable aircraft and get airborne before the response closes in. Flagged missable because it names a single stunt at a single place.

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.guide: The description is a joke with a tank in it: Rhinos are the game's tanks, and this trophy is about dealing with one — most likely taking one on, or taking one over, while the heat is on. The exact act is not spelled out in the official description, so this guide does not invent one: when Rhinos appear at high wanted levels, engage one — destroy it or steal it — and the trophy should follow. Flagged missable because it depends on a tank encounter happening at the right moment, so try it whenever a Rhino shows up rather than waiting for a perfect setup.

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without being detected — a clean, quiet robbery. Plan it like a stealth job: go in when the store is quiet, keep out of sight lines, take what you need and leave before anyone raises the alarm. If you are spotted, the attempt fails, so leave and try again rather than fighting through it — the trophy can be retried as often as needed, which is why it is not flagged missable. Patience is the whole skill here.

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide: Rob 5 bank vaults and escape each time — five successful vault jobs, with the getaway counting as part of the job. Vaults are the big robberies, so expect alarms, police and a chase after each one: plan the escape before you go in, and do not linger. One vault at a time, five times, and the silver is yours. This is the robbery trophy that takes the longest, so start it in Stage 4 and finish it before the final cleanup.

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an armored truck and escape — the classic GTA robbery in miniature. Armored trucks travel the roads of Leonida, so find one on the move, stop it, take the cash and get away before the police close in. A fast car and a quiet stretch of road help, and the escape matters as much as the robbery: losing the wanted level after the hit is what completes the trophy.

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.guide: Explore all of Leonida — all 52 areas, as PSN tracks them. This is the map trophy: visit every named area of the state, from Vice City to the swamps and the coast. Drive the roads, take the side routes, and watch the area counter in the game to see what is left. Fold it into everything else: meditation spots, WAiNK It locations, vehicles and card hunting all take you to new areas, so by the time the other exploration trophies are done this one should be nearly finished too.

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob an illegal operation belonging to each gang — one hit per gang, 9 gangs as PSN tracks them. Gangs run their own rackets around Leonida, so find each gang's operation, rob it and move on to the next. Keep a note of which gangs you have already hit, since the trophy counts gangs, not robberies: hitting the same gang twice earns nothing. Spread the hits across the map and expect each gang's territory to fight back.

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach — the game's quiet moment on the sand. Head to Ocean Beach, find the bar or the spot with the view, order a cocktail and take it in. Nothing to fight and nothing to miss: it can be done at any time, so save it for a breather between the harder trophies. A good one to pair with a sunset drive down the beachfront.

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style — drive a car straight through the showroom glass, the way the old games taught us. Pick a showroom, get a car inside or line one up outside, and drive out through the window. If the first attempt does not trigger it, try another showroom or another angle: the trophy can be retried, and the description asks for the smash itself, not a particular showroom.

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Follow through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley — play a game of bowling there. The trophy names a specific alley, so go to Kolt & Associates, pick up a ball and bowl. It asks for the follow-through, so finish the game rather than walking out halfway. This also counts as one of the activity types for Master of None, and it is the natural partner to Ten Pin (a melee drive-by at the lanes).

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.guide: A partnership with mass appeal — the description is deliberately vague, and this guide will not pretend to know the exact moment: it reads as a story beat where a partnership does something the public notices, most likely a mission or a choice involving both protagonists. Play the story, watch for partnership moments, and keep a save before big story choices so a missed beat can be replayed. Flagged missable because the description ties it to a single partnership moment rather than a repeatable act.

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.guide: Choices made, for better or worse — PSN tracks a count up to 500. This trophy counts the choices you make across the whole game, from dialogue options to story decisions, so it grows naturally as you play and talk to people. Do not rush it: make choices whenever the game offers them, in missions and in the open world, and the count climbs. Flagged missable only in the soft sense — a playthrough that skips dialogue and avoids decisions will reach the finale short of the count, so choose often and keep a save before the biggest story choices.

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.guide: Second time's the charm — succeed at something on your second try after failing it once. The trophy is about the retry itself, so the honest way to earn it is to fail something, then succeed at the same thing right after. Pick a low-stakes challenge you can fail safely (a race, a minigame, a mission objective), fail it once on purpose, then win it on the next attempt. Flagged missable because it needs a first failure followed by a success — a perfect first try everywhere leaves nothing to retry.

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.guide: What the hell just happened? — the description is a question, and this guide will not invent the answer: it reads as a strange, one-off event somewhere in Leonida, the kind of weird encounter this series hides in the corners of the map. Explore odd places, follow strange prompts and keep your eyes open late at night; when something unexplainable happens, the trophy is the game's way of saying you found it. Flagged missable because a one-off event can be walked past and never repeated.

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by — knock people down with a melee attack from a moving vehicle. Drive slowly past a group on foot, swing a melee weapon from the vehicle as you pass, and knock them down. A crowded pavement and a slow car are the setup; speed makes the swing miss, so crawl past and let the melee do the work. It pairs naturally with Let’s Go Bowling at the Kolt & Associates alley.

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Earn $250,000 by laundering Marked Bills through your contacts. Marked Bills are dirty money from robberies and heists, and your contacts clean them for a cut — so this trophy grows out of the robbery trophies: the more vaults, trucks and gang operations you hit, the more marked money you have to launder. Keep laundering as you go rather than hoarding it, and the $250,000 total arrives during the endgame cleanup.

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops — weapons, clothes, cars, food, anything the shops of Leonida sell. This one takes care of itself if you buy gear as you play, but it is easy to finish short if you hoard cash: check the total in the game, and if you are close, spend the difference on something useful — ammo, a car, a wardrobe — rather than letting it sit. It pairs with Dime on the Dollar, since laundered money is money you can spend.

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: Purchase all 8 garage properties — the count is PSN's. Garages are bought with in-game money, so this trophy is a spending goal as much as a property one: earn cash from missions and robberies, then buy each garage as it becomes available. Garages also store the vehicles you discover for Whip It Good and register for On the Spot, so buy them as you go rather than saving them all for the end.

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app. The app is the in-game vehicle service: take vehicles you find to the Scooter Bros app and register them, one by one, until the count hits 10. Use the variety you are already discovering for Whip It Good — any 10 different vehicles will do — and register them as you find them rather than collecting a pile first.
